newsitem.title: FRANCE: Egypt purchase shows U.S. wheat too dear - trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt purchase shows U.S. wheat too dear - trade.

text.p: Egypt bought 600,000 tonnes of wheat over the weekend from countries other than the United States, a move that suggested U.S. prices were out of line with world markets, European grain traders said.

The sale also gave further ammunition to European Union exporters who would like the Commission to stop pricing its wheat against U.S. prices and start competing with cheaper Argentine wheat, they said.
Over the weekend Egypt bought a total of 600,000 tonnes of wheat, with 200,00 tonnes coming from Australia, 250,000 tonnes from Argentina, and 150,000 from France.
U.S. exporters who had hoped to land most of the business with Egypt did not sell a single cargo because their prices were too high, traders said.
French wheat was priced at $149.50-149.85 per tonne, Fob, and was for January loadings.
Argentine wheat for January loadings was sold at $132.50-132.85 per tonne, per tonne, Fob.
Traders noted Argentine prices were in line with expectations and that French wheat had a discount of some five dollars to U.S. wheat.
They also calculated that French wheat showed a premium of some $10 over Argentine wheat on a cost and freight basis.
"Sellers must feel the Commission will have to turn away from pricing its wheat against U.S. wheats and start to compete with Argentine," one grain analyst said.
The EU has until now carefully avoided undercutting U.S. prices to avoid starting a subsidy war with the United States.
But operators have argued higher EU wheat subsidies were needed to help foil competition from Argentina.

Traders calculated the European Commission would have to substantially step up its refund on wheat exports to help cover the French sale, which was made at prices they described as "very competitive".
They estimated refunds of 21 to 26 Ecus were needed to help cover the sale.
Last Thursday at the weekly grain export tender the EU awarded refunds on exports of wheat to third countries at 15.95 Ecus per tonne.
French wheat markets largely ignored news Egypt had bought 150,000 tonnes of French wheat.

Traders noted that although the deal showed a discount of some $10 over last Thursday's EU wheat award, France managed to sell only 150,000 tonnes of wheat to Egypt, a traditional destination for French grain.
"France's share was miserable," one dealer said.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 840 francs per tonne for December delivery and at 820 francs on January-March delivery, both unchanged from Friday. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
